text:
Patrick Kane came home to Chicago at 38, with three Stanley Cups, a Hart Trophy and 1,400 career points behind him, and the second act has been quiet. He has one goal in 18 games and none in his last 17, on 4.2 expected goals (the quality of his chances). His shooting is at 2.9% against a league average of 13.4%, which is not sustainable in either direction: the goals should come.

The harder part is the rest of the picture. The Blackhawks have just 39% of the expected goals at five on five with him on the ice, his minutes are down nearly three a night over the last 10 games, and his skating numbers sit near the middle of the league. He still sees the ice like few do: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 10.3 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 95th percentile among forwards.

With Connor Bedard out with a shoulder injury and the Blackhawks weighing rehab or surgery, Kane sits on the top power-play unit and the team needs his passing more than ever. Watch for the first goal; the chances say it isn't far off.
